confusions: The debt page gives two different debt figures (IMF and OECD) with a note that neither is the only correct one, and I did not know which to go by.
On the tax and income pages, 46.0% and 36.2% are both about the richest fifth, one a share of all taxes and one a share of income, and I could not keep them apart.
The class size section has lots of close numbers (26.3, 21.5, 23.1, 26.4) and a Scotland figure, so I could not tell which one was the England primary figure.
The Work section shows one overall employment chart with no 18 to 24 or 25 to 34 figures that I could find, so I gave up looking for them.
The housing ownership chart is a dotted line with no clear 2008-09 figure I could read, so I could not work out the change.
The borrowing-cost page is long text and I skimmed past the quotes about what moves borrowing costs, so I did not get the list of factors.
The top 1% and wealth-tax questions were not answered in what I read, and I ran out of actions before reaching defence, migration, welfare, OECD and debt-history pages.
